Other condition: The research proposal must fall under the remit of the Leverhulme Centre for Life in the Universe. Research within the Centre aims to develop a deeper understanding of life, its emergence, and its distribution in the Universe by addressing four research themes:; What are the chemical pathways which led to the origins of life that are compatible with benign conditions for life in different planetary environments?; How do we characterise the environments on Earth and other planets that could act as the cradle of prebiotic chemistry and life?; What observational facilities and methods will allow investigation of bodies beyond the Solar System, the remote sensing of their atmospheres and the search for signatures of geological and biological evolution?; How can philosophical and mathematical concepts refine our understanding of what we mean by life, leading to new interdisciplinary collaborations and modes of scientific enquiry?

record.about: The CAM Doctoral Training Partnership [DTP] is a consortium including Anglia Ruskin University, the University of Bedfordshire and the University of Cambridge, funded by the Economic and Social Research Council [ESRC]. CAM-DTP attracts talented doctoral researchers from a wide range of backgrounds and social science disciplines (see ESRC social science disciplines for more information). An ESRC-funded PhD studentship award provides maintenance [£21,805 per annum in 2026-27] and University of Cambridge Postgraduate Fees at the Home rate. We are especially keen to see applications that involve: ESRC Steers: Advanced Quantitative Methods, Data Skills, Interdisciplinary CAM-DTP Collabs: Knowledge Exchange, Cross-Departmental, Cross-CAM, Cross-DTP Please see the CAM-DTP website for more details ﻿ Nominations can be through our advertised studentships or through departmental selection of strong applications fitting the ESRC remit. Please see the CAM-DTP website for the current list of advertised studentships. CAM-DTP PhD students have access to grants for additional training costs and may apply for further discretionary funding to contribute to fieldwork costs, academic exchange, and collaboration with non-academic organisations. Studentships are available to UK and international candidates. Although the CAM-DTP application portal is open to all University of Cambridge PhD applicants, only those also nominated by their Faculty/Department will be reviewed and considered for funding. Faculties/Departments will automatically consider all eligible applicants who have applied for admission by the appropriate funding deadline; Deadlines are specific to the course you are applying to - please refer to the funding deadline provided for your course in the Postgraduate Prospectus; Any queries should be directed to the Faculty/Department in the first instance. Awards will be offered during the period April to July 2027 via departments. If you have not had any correspondence by 1 August 2027 you may assume you have been unsuccessful. Awards cannot be deferred to the following academic year. This fund welcomes nominations for applicants who have faced disadvantage, or come from underrepresented backgrounds, to access postgraduate study at Cambridge.

record.about: The University of Cambridge is one of 50 UK institutions selected by the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) to join the Doctoral Landscape Awards (DLA) programme, launched in autumn 2026. Through the DLA grant, Cambridge offers three fully funded PhD studentships per year , covering tuition fees, a maintenance stipend, and a research training support grant. In addition, the University has committed to funding three further studentships annually , expanding opportunities for outstanding researchers. Applicants must pursue research primarily in the arts and humanities; interdisciplinary projects with a strong arts & humanities core are also encouraged. Cambridge is part of the London and East of England AHRC DLA Hub (LEAH DLA Hub), a regional network promoting collaboration, training, and the sharing of best practices across participating institutions. This partnership will help shape the future of arts and humanities research across the region. This fund is designated to support applicants who have faced disadvantage, or come from underrepresented backgrounds, to access postgraduate study at Cambridge. We particularly welcome applications from people who identify as coming from an underrepresented ethnic background (Black - Caribbean or Caribbean British; Black - African or African British; Asian - Pakistani or Pakistani British; Asian - Bangladeshi or British Bangladeshi) or having experienced educational disadvantage. The Cambridge AHRC DLA offers up to two studentships dedicated to support inclusion.

record.about: The Cambridge Biosciences DTP is a four year PhD programme that aims to create highly skilled and employable people. The programme offers training across 23 University Departments/Institutes and 3 Partner Institutes providing access to a wide range of research areas related to the strategic themes of the BBSRC. We offer two types of DTP studentships: Targeted iCase You can choose to select up to two projects, these projects can be from the same or different research areas and can be any combination of project types, including two Targeted projects, two iCASE projects, or one of each. For each project you select, you will need to provide a short statement explaining your interest in the project. This should include: What interests you about the project; Any discussions you have had with the project supervisor, if applicable; and Relevant projects, experience or coursework that have prepared you for this research area. You will need to apply through the University’s Applicant Portal. The course is listed as PhD in Biological Sciences.

record.about: Funder: EPSRC via the Centre for Doctoral Training in Materials 4.0 Duration: 4 years (start October 2027) Fee status: home rate fees only, a fee waiver bursary for overseas fee payers may be available Supervisor: Will depend on student project selection Closing date: 13 May 2027 This studentship is offered under the umbrella of the Materials 4.0 Centre for Doctoral Training (CDT) led by the Henry Royce Institute, the UK’s national institute for advanced materials research. Right now, our society faces huge, urgent challenges. From the imperative to achieve net-zero, to the need to build a resilient, circular economy in an uncertain world, to the drive for increased productivity as our fellow nations embrace the digital revolution. To tackle these challenges, we need new materials and new materials systems, and we need them fast. But it can take 20 years to develop a new material with current methods. We need to innovate faster, as the pace of global change accelerates. This is where you come in…… We are seeking graduate scientists and engineers keen to acquire new skills and work in new ways, to help us realise the potential of the digital and data revolutions in materials science. This is Materials 4.0. · You will join a community of like-minded PhD researchers as part of a new EPSRC-funded CDT in Materials 4.0, led by the Henry Royce Institute, the UK’s national institute for advanced materials research. · You will be based at Cambridge University and undertake a research project supervised by a leading researcher and with an industry sponsor. · You will be trained in all aspects of digital materials science, including robotics, data science, machine learning, and sensing and control. · You will become a pioneer and leader in this exciting new way of doing science. We have a range of exciting doctoral projects, involving all aspects of Materials 4.0, and offer flexible and inclusive pathways, including part-time study. Informal enquiries may be made by email to Professor Rachel Oliver, rao28@cam.ac.uk . Applications are made through the 'applicant portal' at https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/ . Further information on the application process is available from Dr Rosie Ward ( remw2@cam.ac.uk ). We reserve the right to fill the position with a qualified candidate prior to the conclusion of the advertising period. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

record.about: Founded in 2007, the Loke Centre for Trophoblast Research (Loke CTR) brings together 30 Principal Investigators with a shared interest in the scientific study of the placenta, early development and maternal-fetal interactions during pregnancy. Our PIs are recognized international experts in their fields based across Cambridge in the Departments of Physiology, Development, and Neuroscience , Obstetrics and Gynaecology , Pathology , Genetics , and allied institutes, including the Institute of Metabolic Science , Cambridge Stem Cell Institute , Cambridge Institute of Therapeutic Immunology and Infectious Disease , the LMB , Babraham , and Wellcome Sanger Institute . A Loke CTR Studentship will be held within the relevant Department or Institute, where an internal Departmental Postgraduate Educational Committee is responsible for administering your degree. The Loke CTR offers one fully-funded 4-year PhD studentship at home or overseas rates. Eligible P hD projects are advertised on our website. Each project is jointly supervised by two Loke CTR research groups, providing interdisciplinary PhD training in placental and reproductive biology.

record.results_date: The Trust’s awarding period runs from the middle of February to the end of July and is an ongoing process throughout that period. Most of our awards are made early during the months of February and March, but some of our partner funded awards involve additional processes such as interviews, which means funding decisions tend to be later from April to June. Although we cannot provide funding updates for individual applicants, the Trust will confirm on our website once we have finished issuing offers for our main scholarship programmes. Throughout the awarding period the Trust will be reallocating awards that have not been taken up. Therefore, all applicants will remain under consideration for any reallocated award for which they are eligible until the end of July. If you have not been contacted by the Trust by the end of July, you should assume that your funding application has not been successful.

record.about: AstraZeneca Non-Clinical PhD Studentship Programme: Development of an Integrated Pre-Clinical Pipeline for Safety Assessment of Small Molecule and Peptide-Based Radioconjugates Using In Vivo PET Imaging and Multimodal Ex Vivo Tissue Analysis The Department of Radiology at the University of Cambridge, in partnership with AstraZeneca, is offering a funded PhD studentship to develop innovative approaches for the safety assessment of next-generation radiopharmaceuticals. We are seeking a motivated, enthusiastic and inquisitive student with an interest in molecular imaging, radiopharmaceutical sciences, oncology, translational medicine and drug development. The successful candidate will join a highly multidisciplinary team, supervised by Professor Luigi Aloj (Department of Radiology), Dr Flaviu Bulat (Department of Radiology), Dr Nisha Kuzhuppilly Ramakrishnan (Department of Clinical Neurosciences), and Dr Andreas Dannhorn (AstraZeneca), and gain experience working across both academic and industrial research environments. The student could have a background in a wide range of relevant research areas, for example: imaging, biology, biochemistry, chemistry, biomedical sciences, pharmaceutical sciences, data analysis, or medicine. Project Description Targeted radionuclide therapy is an emerging and highly promising approach for cancer treatment. Radioconjugates combine tumour-targeting molecules with therapeutic radioisotopes, enabling the selective delivery of radiation to cancer cells while minimising damage to healthy tissue. Despite recent clinical successes, there remains a significant need for improved methods to evaluate how these compounds distribute throughout the body and to better understand potential toxicities in normal organs. This project aims to establish an integrated preclinical framework for the assessment of small molecule and peptide-based radioconjugates using advanced molecular imaging and tissue analysis techniques. A key objective will be to integrate imaging and tissue-derived data to create a versatile and translatable safety assessment pipeline that can be applied across multiple radiopharmaceutical platforms. The resulting framework will help improve understanding of off-target effects, support the optimisation of emerging targeted radionuclide therapies and contribute to the safer translation of new cancer treatments into clinical development. The student will receive training in and develop expertise in radiochemistry, radiolabelling, quantitative biodistribution studies and PET imaging, using these techniques to investigate the distribution of radioconjugates in preclinical models. The project will combine non-invasive imaging approaches with complementary ex vivo analyses, including autoradiography, histopathology and advanced spatial tissue profiling methodologies such as mass spectrometry imaging, to provide a comprehensive understanding of tissue exposure and early indicators of toxicity. record.about: This four-year studentship is funded by Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute and includes full funding for University fees and an index-linked stipend starting at £22,894 per annum for four years. Supervisor Dr Hamid Raza Ali wishes to recruit a student to work on the project entitled: “Discovery of rational therapeutic biomarkers in breast cancer by systems pathology and deep learning”. Applications are invited from graduates in quantitative disciplines such as computer science, AI, and mathematics, but we also encourage applications from biologists and clinicians already experienced in computational methods. We welcome applications from both UK and overseas students. You must visit this page for full project details before applying: https://www.cam.ac.uk/jobs/fully-funded-phd-studentship-discovery-of-rational-therapeutic-biomarkers-in-breast-cancer-by-sw50984 For further information about the research group, including their most recent publications, please visit their website at www.ali-lab.co.uk/ If you are interested in finding out more about our groundbreaking scientific research, please visit our website at https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/ To be eligible for consideration for this funding, please apply via the University Applicant Portal. Shortlisting will take place after the studentship application deadline (16th October 2026) and we expect to hold interviews in early January 2027. Applicants will be informed of the results by February 2027. For further information about the course and to access the Applicant Portal, visit: https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/cvcrpdmsc You should select to commence study in October 2027. Note about references: We would appreciate it if you could ask your referees to submit their references as soon as possible upon request, despite the longer University deadline for references. They will receive a request once you have completed the References section of your application.
record.results_date: Interviews are planned to take place in the week beginning 4th January 2027, with results expected to be available by February 2027.

record.about: The University is a lead or partner in 7 of the EPSRC Centres for Doctoral Training (CDTs) which started in October 2024. Each CDT will support a minimum of 50 studentships over five years of recruitment. The FIBE3 CDT, in close partnership with its industry partners, aims to develop the next generation of PhD graduates to champion the urgent, complex, inter-connected and cross-disciplinary transition to net zero infrastructure. Students' potential will be transformed by equipping them with the knowledge, skills and qualities to collaboratively engineer the infrastructure that will unlock net zero. Through conducting world-class, cutting-edge and user-need focused cohort-based training and research, FIBE3 CDT students will gain the knowledge and skills required to lead the design and implementation of the infrastructure net zero agenda in the UK. The studentships are fully funded (fees and maintenance at the UKRI rate) for all four years of the course. The majority of awards are made to Home students, but up to 30% may be made to International (including EU) students. International students receiving UKRI funding are automatically eligible for the University Fee Bursary Scheme to cover the difference between the Home and International fee rates. Please see our website for more detailed information and how to apply: https://www.net-zero-fibe-cdt.eng.cam.ac.uk/

record.about: This four-year doctoral training programme in Aerosol Science is part of the multi-institutional EPSRC Aerosol Science Centre for Doctoral Training (CDT) and aims to provide scientists and engineers with a broad overview of the aerosol science sector in addition to in-depth training in detailed measurements, analysis and application approaches. The initial full-time training phase of the doctoral training programme is aimed at building skills through taking taught courses at the University of Bristol, followed by a thematic broadening research placement that allows for complementary skills building. The taught courses provide training in the underlying physical science governing the properties and transformation of aerosols. Final research projects are agreed upon at the start of the PhD and will be advertised for students to select. Training within the initial phase will provide the student with skills enabling: the acquisition of a broad understanding of core aerosol topics, as well as transferable skills in a substantial body of knowledge which is at the forefront of an academic aerosol discipline or area of aerosol professional practice; the creation and interpretation of new knowledge, through original research or other advanced scholarship, of a quality to satisfy peer review, extend the forefront of the discipline, and merit publication; the development of a PhD thesis for an examination that they can defend in an oral examination. This CDT operates in collaboration with the Universities of Bristol, Bath, Birmingham, Hertfordshire, Imperial College London, Surrey and Manchester. The majority of awards are made to Home students, but up to 30% may be made to International (including EU) students. International students receiving UKRI funding are automatically eligible for the University Fee Bursary Scheme to cover the difference between the Home and International fee rates. Full fellowship available for PhD candidates satisfying Widening Participation goals. Please see the Aerosol Science CDT website for more detailed information: Aerosol Science CDT | Centre for Doctoral Training in Aerosol Science .

record.about: EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Awards (previously known as Doctoral Training Partnership awards) enable departments to support doctoral students across a wide range of Engineering and Physical Science research areas . Due to the flexible nature of the Landscape funding, the number of studentships available each year vary as Departments may leverage other funding opportunities, e.g. with Industry Partners, Colleges and other University funding. Studentships are fully-funded at the Home fee rate and UKRI stipend level. Funding for consumable costs, and training (which is an integral part of all doctoral studentships), are also provided. Up to 30% of our awards may be made to international students. All eligible candidates will be considered for this funding. Applicants do not need to indicate that they would like to be considered for a Landscape Award. Students from groups currently under-represented in Engineering and Physical Science subjects are particularly encouraged to apply. Further information can be found at https://www.epsrc.group.cam.ac.uk/DTP/dla-funding . In addition to the skills gained during the PhD research, students also undertake a Researcher Development programme, with courses and activities tailored to their needs and selected from a wide range of provision. This equips those completing their doctoral programmes to develop the broad skill set which will make them well-placed to develop into future leaders across a range of careers in the academic, industrial and public sectors.

Please note that contacting us to request an update cannot lead to a quicker decision, so we ask that you are patient and wait to hear from us until that point. If you have not heard from us by the end of April, please assume that your funding application has not been successful. For the same reason, it is not possible to provide individual feedback to applicants. There are a limited number of awards available, and applications are considered on the basis of academic merit, taking into account contextual factors, and available departmental resources, including supervisors and suitable projects.

record.about: If you are a citizen of the United States and currently resident in the United States, please apply for Gates Cambridge (US Round) instead. Each year Gates Cambridge offers c. 75 full-cost scholarships to outstanding applicants from countries outside the UK to pursue a postgraduate degree in any subject available at the University of Cambridge. These awards are split between two rounds, one for US citizens residing in the US, and another for all other eligible applicants. Approximately 20 of the 75 awards are available in the US round, and the remaining 55 are available in the international round. In terms of the split between PhD and MPhil students, about two-thirds of the total 75 awards are offered to PhD students. There are at least 225 Gates Cambridge Scholars from c. 50 countries studying in Cambridge at any one time who pursue the full range of subjects available at the University and are spread across its departments and Colleges. The Gates Cambridge mission is to build a global network of future leaders committed to improving the lives of others. It aims to achieve this mission by selecting outstanding scholars, providing them with support at one of the world’s leading universities, and facilitating community building at and beyond Cambridge.

record.about: Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholarships provide the most talented PhD students with life-changing opportunities to research and study at the University of Cambridge. The Programme offers generous fully-funded Scholarships, which include fees at the Home or Overseas rate. These Scholarships support PhD students from any part of the world, and in any discipline. All applicants who are assessed as being academically excellent by their Department or Faculty are eligible to be considered for an award. Students applying for '1+3' model courses are eligible for consideration. The Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholars Programme (HDPSP) was established in February 2019 thanks to an extraordinarily generous donation from the David and Claudia Harding Foundation, the biggest single gift made to a university in the UK by a British philanthropist.

record.about: The Herchel Smith Research Studentships are prestigious University of Cambridge awards supporting outstanding PhD candidates in organic chemistry and related areas of the molecular life sciences . Herchel Smith Students become part of an active academic community of students and postdoctoral fellows, with opportunities to engage across disciplines and develop connections with researchers at Cambridge and Harvard. As part of the programme, students are expected to participate actively in Herchel Smith community activities, including meetings, research presentations, poster sessions and the annual Herchel Smith Symposium. Students may also have the opportunity to take part in the Harvard Lab Exchange Programme , spending two to three months at Harvard University undertaking research that complements and broadens their PhD experience. The Herchel Smith Studentship Managers organise a range of academic and community activities for researchers participating in the Cambridge and Harvard programmes. There is no separate application process for the Herchel Smith Studentship. Eligible candidates applying for PhD study in relevant departments are considered for nomination by their department. Nominations are then considered by the Herchel Smith Studentship Managers, with awards made on the basis of academic excellence. Herchel Smith PhD Studentships are available only through selected Cambridge Colleges that participate in the Herchel Smith co-funding programme .

record.about: This four-year studentship is funded by Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute and includes full funding for University fees and an index-linked stipend starting at £22,894 per annum for four years. Supervisor Dr Tim Halim welcomes applications from UK and overseas students with the following preferred skills and knowledge: Cell biology / Immunology laboratory experience, such as: Flow cytometry and FACS, immunofluorescence microscopy/imaging, cell culture, tumour cell killing assays, tissue processing, etc. Molecular biology laboratory experience, such as: DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, cloning, virus production, ELISA, etc. Computational biology laboratory experience, such as: bulk- singl cell- or spatial-transcriptomic data analysis, spatial biology analysis using HALO, Imaris, etc. Murine or human tissue work, such as: tissue processing, tumour or immune-related in vivo models, surgical skills, transgenic animal models, UK PIL training, etc. Knowledge: background in cancer biology, immunology, cell biology, etc. Training and interest in bioinformatics, computational biology. You must visit this page for full project details before applying: https://www.cam.ac.uk/jobs/fully-funded-phd-studentship-innate-adaptive-immune-interactions-in-cancer-evolution-sw51021 For further information about the research group, including their most recent publications, please visit our website at https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/research-groups/halim-group/ If you are interested in finding out more about our groundbreaking scientific research, please visit our website at https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/ To be eligible for consideration for this funding, please apply via the University Applicant Portal. Shortlisting will take place after the studentship application deadline (16th October 2026) and we expect to hold interviews in early January 2027. Applicants will be informed of the results by February 2027. For further information about the course and to access the Applicant Portal, visit: https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/cvcrpdmsc You should select to commence study in October 2027. Note about references: We would appreciate it if you could ask your referees to submit their references as soon as possible upon request, despite the longer University deadline for references. They will receive a request once you have completed the References section of your application.
record.results_date: Interviews are planned to take place in the week beginning 4th January 2027, with results expected to be available by February 2027.

record.about: The University of Cambridge expects to offer at least fifteen 3.5 year NERC-funded PhD studentships through the Cambridge Research Experience and Advanced Training for Environmental Scientists (CREATES) DLA to start 1 October 2027. UK students will be eligible for a full Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) studentship. The standard terms and conditions for UKRI training funding and related guidance can be found here . A full studentship will cover the cost of fees plus the standard UKRI maintenance allowance (for 2026/27 this is £21,805 pa). The CREATES NERC DLA will be able to offer a limited number of studentships to international students (EU and non-EU), and funding from UKRI will cover fees at the UK rate and the standard maintenance allowance to support living costs. For those who are successful in winning a DLA studentship, the University of Cambridge will currently offer a waiver to cover the difference in cost between International and UK fees. More information about fee status is available on the university website . The CREATES NERC DLA and University of Cambridge actively support equality, diversity and inclusion and we encourage applications from eligible applicants from all sections of society. To be considered for this studentship, Applicants must tick the box 'I wish to apply for funding' on the Application Portal and meet the eligibility criteria. For further details, including funding and eligibility information, please see the Cambridge NERC Doctoral Training Partnerships pages , including how to apply and the NERC website . If you have any questions, we're happy to help. Contact Ruth Noble, CREATES DLA Administrator at dtp-admin@esc.cam.ac.uk or the departmental Postgraduate Administrators for your chosen project(s).

record.about: We invite applications from creative and motivated individuals to join Professor Sir Shankar Balasubramanian’s group for a 4-year PhD studentship, working on multidisciplinary projects exploiting both chemistry and biology to explore fundamental mechanisms of genome function ( http://www.balasubramanian.co.uk ). Our projects develop and use cutting edge technologies in chemical biology, molecular biophysics, structural biology and genomics to answer critical questions in genome function. Students will contribute to one or more of our primary research areas below: A key interest is the structure and function of DNA secondary structures called G-quadruplexes (G4s). G4s are important in gene and chromatin regulation and our aims are to use chemical biology strategies to elucidate their role in genome biology and to develop small molecule-based intervention strategies for cancer [e.g. see Genome Biology, 2025 , 25 , 155; Nature Chemistry, 2025 , 17 , 875; PNAS , 2024 , 12(7) , e2320240121; Nature Communications , 2022 , 13 :142; Genome Biology , 2021 , 22 , 117] We are also developing techniques to map where small molecules bind to DNA and chromatin and to identify the proteins associated with their binding sites with a view to understanding therapeutic mechanisms [e.g. see Nature Biotechnology , 2023 , 41 , 1265]. Our aim is to characterise small molecule interactions with DNA, RNA and associated proteins and to enable the development of bifunctional small molecules that target the genome and chromatin-associated proteins to understand genome mechanisms and explore their therapeutic potential in diseases such as cancer. The design of bifunctional modalities will encompass new modalities of proximity-inducers that target contextual biology. A recent example being degraders that act at G-quadruplex locations in chromatin [e.g. see Nature Chemistry, 2026 , 18 , 1092]. This position will be primarily based in the Balasubramanian lab at the Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry and will involve collaborative interactions with the group’s sister lab at the CRUK Cambridge Institute. The student will be highly motivated, capable of independent thought and have excellent communication skills with the ability to work collaboratively. Ideally, the candidate will have a strong background in biochemistry/chemistry and/or molecular biology. A good knowledge of genomics and the chemistry/chemical biology of nucleic acids is highly desirable. The studentship commences in October 2027 and provides a maintenance grant and tuition fees at the UK rate. However, we could support outstanding overseas students in their application for a suitable scholarship. Interviews will take place on Wednesday 11 th November 2026 . For queries regarding the studentship, please contact Jo at BalasubramanianRecruitment@ch.cam.ac.uk.

record.about: Applications are invited for a PhD studentship (home or international) in chemical engineering under the supervision of Professor Erwin Reisner within the Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry at the University of Cambridge. The studentship targets the top candidates worldwide to join our international research team and on a 3.5-year scholarship starting in October 2027. The Reisner Laboratory develops innovative technologies to convert solar energy into sustainable fuels and organic platform chemicals for a circular economy using a unique cross-disciplinary and collaborative approach. Working with and learning from an experienced team of cross-disciplinary scientists and engineers, the PhD student will develop a scalable process for photoreforming technology, which uses solar energy to upcycle plastic waste into fuel such as hydrogen gas and valuable organic chemicals. The PhD student will work together with chemistry and materials experts and design continuous-flow solar reactors to demonstrate this solar chemical technology at a kg plastic and metre square scale under real sunlight irradiation. This project supports a Royal Academy of Engineering Chair in Emerging Technologies programme to enable the practical deployment of solar chemical technologies. The outcome of this project is expected to be published in top tier academic journals and generate novel IP to support the commercial aspirations of this project. More information about the laboratory and project can be found here: Website Reisner Laboratory Publication on metre square scale photoreforming Review solar reforming technology For any queries, please contact Gioia Gregori at pa-reisner@ch.cam.ac.uk .

The studentship targets the top candidates worldwide to join our international research team and on a 4-year scholarship starting in October 2027. The Reisner Laboratory develops innovative technologies to convert solar energy into sustainable fuels and organic platform chemicals for a circular economy using a unique cross-disciplinary and collaborative approach. Working with and learning from an experienced team of cross-disciplinary scientists, the PhD student will engineer live cells to convert carbon dioxide and other feedstock chemicals into bespoke complex chemicals. record.about: Applications are invited for a PhD studentship (home or international) in photocatalytic air-to-fuel conversion under the supervision of Professor Erwin Reisner within the Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry at the University of Cambridge. The studentship targets the top candidates worldwide to join our international research team and on a 3.5 year scholarship starting in October 2027. The Reisner Laboratory develops innovative technologies to convert solar energy into sustainable fuels and organic platform chemicals for a circular economy using a unique cross-disciplinary and collaborative approach. Working with and learning from an experienced team of cross-disciplinary scientists, the PhD student will develop practical integrated systems for the capture and subsequent utilisation of atmospheric CO2 to produce green fuels and valuable chemicals. The focus will be on developing photocatalytic systems for gas-phase CO2 conversion to products and optimising these systems for integration with carbon capture processes. The PhD student will work with other PhD students and postdocs experienced in carbon capture and conversion, and the project will build upon previous work in the group and utilise the broad expertise within the group. The emphasis is on direct air capture, the coupling of carbon capture and solar-driven conversion, sunlight concentration, outdoor testing, as well as broad-spectrum light utilisation. This research will thereby develop carbon capture and utilisation technologies, and the research is part of a wider collaborative UK research network on the development of solar air-to-fuel technologies. The outcome is expected to be published in top tier academic journals and the potential generation of novel IP. More information about the laboratory and project can be found here: Reisner Laboratory Website Publication on direct air capture and gas-phase CO2 conversion Review on solar air-to-fuel technologies For any queries, please contact Gioia Gregori at pa-reisner@ch.cam.ac.uk.

record.results_date: The Trust’s awarding period runs from the middle of February to the end of July and is an ongoing process throughout that period. Most of our awards are made early during the months of February and March, but some of our partner funded awards involve additional processes such as interviews, which means funding decisions tend to be later from April to June. Although we cannot provide funding updates for individual applicants, the Trust will confirm on our website once we have finished issuing offers for our main scholarship programmes. Throughout the awarding period the Trust will be reallocating awards that have not been taken up. Therefore, all applicants will remain under consideration for any reallocated award for which they are eligible until the end of July. If you have not been contacted by the Trust by the end of July, you should assume that your funding application has not been successful.

record.about: This four-year studentship is funded by Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute and includes full funding for University fees and an index-linked stipend starting at £22,894 per annum for four years. Supervisor Dr Guiping Wang is looking for a curious, motivated and collaborative student with an interest in interdisciplinary science at the intersection of molecular biology, genomics, microscopy and computation. Applicants should hold, or expect to gain, an undergraduate or Master's degree in biophysics, biology, physics, chemistry, bioengineering, physical chemistry, biomedical sciences, or a related discipline. Any of the following experience would be helpful, although we do not expect any one applicant to have all of it: Laboratory experience in molecular or cell biology – for example mammalian cell culture, nucleic acid work, or immunofluorescence staining. Hands-on experience of fluorescence microscopy, or of optics and instrument building. Exposure to next-generation sequencing, either at the bench or in analysis. Programming in Python, R or MATLAB, and any experience of analysing image or sequencing data. A previous research project, internship or Master's thesis in a related area. We welcome applications from both UK and overseas students. You must visit this page for full project details before applying: https://www.cam.ac.uk/jobs/fully-funded-phd-studentship-single-cell-spatial-multi-omics-for-cancer-biology-sw51030 For further information about the research group, including its most recent publications, please visit our website at https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/research-groups/wang-group/ If you are interested in finding out more about our groundbreaking scientific research, please visit our website at https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/ To be eligible for consideration for this funding, please apply via the University Applicant Portal. Shortlisting will take place after the studentship application deadline (16th October 2026) and we expect to hold interviews in early January 2027. Applicants will be informed of the results by February 2027. For further information about the course and to access the Applicant Portal, visit: https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/cvcrpdmsc You should select to commence study in October 2027. Note about references: We would appreciate it if you could ask your referees to submit their references as soon as possible upon request, despite the longer University deadline for references. They will receive a request once you have completed the References section of your application.

record.results_date: The Trust’s awarding period runs from the middle of February to the end of July and is an ongoing process throughout that period. Most of our awards are made early during the months of February and March, but some of our partner funded awards involve additional processes such as interviews, which means funding decisions tend to be later from April to June. Although we cannot provide funding updates for individual applicants, the Trust will confirm on our website once we have finished issuing offers for our main scholarship programmes. Throughout the awarding period the Trust will be reallocating awards that have not been taken up. Therefore, all applicants will remain under consideration for any reallocated award for which they are eligible until the end of July. If you have not been contacted by the Trust by the end of July, you should assume that your funding application has not been successful.

record.about: This four-year studentship is funded by Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute and includes full funding for University fees and an index-linked stipend starting at £22,894 per annum for four years. Prof Masashi Narita wishes to recruit a student to work on the project entitled: “Understanding the identity and function of tumour-initiating states”. Previous hands-on laboratory research experience is highly desirable. Experience in one or more of the following would be advantageous but is not essential: mammalian cell culture, molecular biology, microscopy, genetic manipulation, chromatin or epigenetic assays, and cancer or ageing model systems. The successful candidate should have a strong interest in mechanistic biology and in using experimental approaches to understand fundamental questions in cancer development. Computational or bioinformatics expertise is advantageous but not required. Training and collaborative support will be available to analyse genomic datasets generated during the project. We welcome applications from both UK and overseas students. You must visit this page for full project details before applying: https://www.cam.ac.uk/jobs/fully-funded-phd-studentship-understanding-the-identity-and-function-of-tumour-initiating-states-sw51026 For further information about the research group, including their most recent publications, please visit their website at https://www.naritalab.com/ If you are interested in finding out more about our groundbreaking scientific research, please visit our website at https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/ To be eligible for consideration for this funding, please apply via the University Applicant Portal. Shortlisting will take place after the studentship application deadline (16th October 2026) and we expect to hold interviews in early January 2027. Applicants will be informed of the results by February 2027. For further information about the course and to access the Applicant Portal, visit: https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/cvcrpdmsc You should select to commence study in October 2027. Note about references: We would appreciate it if you could ask your referees to submit their references as soon as possible upon request, despite the longer University deadline for references. They will receive a request once you have completed the References section of your application.
record.results_date: Interviews are planned to take place in the week beginning 4th January 2027, with results expected to be available by February 2027.

record.about: This four-year studentship is funded by Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute and includes full funding for University fees and an index-linked stipend starting at £22,894 per annum for four years. Supervisor Dr Giulia Biffi is looking for a motivated student who is excited by this project, enthusiastic about joining a collaborative and hard-working laboratory, and committed to the complementary experimental strategies required for its successful completion. As this project will rely heavily on mouse models, willingness to work with mouse models throughout the PhD is essential. Prior experience in a laboratory or industry research environment is required. Experience with tissue culture, including cell lines and/or organoids, common laboratory techniques such as immunohistochemistry, western blotting and/or PCR, and work with mouse models would be viewed favourably. Prior experience or knowledge of pancreatic cancer or cancer biology would also be advantageous. We welcome applications from both UK and overseas students. You must visit this page for full project details before applying: https://www.cam.ac.uk/jobs/fully-funded-phd-studentship-unmasking-mechanisms-of-resistance-to-kras-inhibition-across-pancreatic-sw51012 For further information about the research group, including their most recent publications, please visit their website at https://biffilab.wordpress.com If you are interested in finding out more about our groundbreaking scientific research, please visit our website at https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/ To be eligible for consideration for this funding, please apply via the University Applicant Portal. Shortlisting will take place after the studentship application deadline (16th October 2026) and we expect to hold interviews in early January 2027. Applicants will be informed of the results by February 2027. For further information about the course and to access the Applicant Portal, visit: https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/cvcrpdmsc You should select to commence study in October 2027. Note about references: We would appreciate it if you could ask your referees to submit their references as soon as possible upon request, despite the longer University deadline for references. They will receive a request once you have completed the References section of your application.
record.results_date: Interviews are planned to take place in the week beginning 4th January 2027, with results expected to be available by February 2027.

record.about: Wakefield Scholarships are for persons intending to pursue a course of advanced study or research at the Institute of Criminology. Scholarships are awarded from the benefaction of Mrs Priscilla Mitchell (née Wakefield) in memory of her brother, Captain Edward Roger Wakefield, and also in recognition of the historic work of her forebears, Edward Gibbon Wakefield, Daniel Bell Wakefield, William Hayward Wakefield, and Arthur Wakefield in the development of New Zealand, South Australia, and Canada in the nineteenth century. Wakefield Scholarships are open to any person who was born or educated in Australia, Canada, or New Zealand. If two or more candidates born or educated in Australia are equally well qualified, preference is given to a candidate who was born or educated in South Australia. Scholarships are awarded annually, but Wakefield Scholars are eligible for re-election, provided that the tenure of a Scholarship does not normally exceed three years in all. The value of the Wakefield Scholarship is determined by the course of study: PhD: One award of £20,000 towards University Composition Fees and/or maintenance. record.about: The Williams Papworth Studentship provides full or partial support for students from the Tibetan Plateau or surrounding countries or regions. Preference may be given to applicants who are ethnically or culturally connected with the Himalayan region. The studentship is normally available for one-year postgraduate courses. Consideration will be given only in exceptional circumstances to those seeking support for PhDs or who have spent extended periods of time studying in universities in Western Europe, USA, Canada or Australia. The Studentship seeks to support students committed to the practical application of knowledge and/or the development of ideas. The potential of the applicant to make a significant, positive and forward-looking contribution to his/her own community and the wider world is overall more important than the subject of study, ethnicity or religious affiliation. Past students have studied Criminology, Veterinary Science, Conservation Leadership, Linguistics and Education. Applications from those wishing to study other academic disciples are also welcome although preference will not normally be given to those wishing to study Social Anthropology. Premium rate courses are not included. The Studentship is tenable at any College. This scholarship is offered in partnership with Bill and Hilary Papworth.

record.about: Applications are invited for W.M. Tapp Studentships in Law for PhD study for 2027 entry. The value of the Studentship will be determined after considering successful candidates’ income from other sources. Approved University and College fees will be paid, together with a maintenance award which satisfies the University Postgraduate Admissions Office’s conditions for entry as a postgraduate student. An additional college scholarship of £500 per annum is paid. A contribution may also be made towards expenses incurred when travelling to the UK if the student's home country is overseas. An allowance may be paid for dependents, and grants are available for research expenses. Tenure of a W.M. Tapp Studentship in Law is conditional upon the successful applicant(s) being accepted by the University Postgraduate Admissions Office. Candidates must be graduates in Law of any university in the United Kingdom or elsewhere or be about to graduate not later than 1 September of the year they commence studying at Cambridge. They will be expected to be of outstanding academic ability and first consideration will be given to candidates who nominate Gonville & Caius College as their first preference college. An application form is available from the college website. Two supporting references are also required. These should be Tapp-specific and indicate your academic fitness and suitability to undertake your proposed course or research. Completed application forms, transcripts and references should be submitted no later than, 23:59 (UK time) 5 January 2027, before starting the following October.

lines: Postgraduate scholarships
Every year, Newnham offers scholarships for students about to register for an MPhil or PhD. The scholarships available for entry in October 2027 are listed below.
Applications

To be eligible for a Newnham scholarship you must be an applicant for a new postgraduate course. Students who have already begun their course are not eligible unless they are applying for a new course (e.g. an MPhil student applying for a PhD).

Applicants must indicate that they wish to be considered for funding when applying for their course through the Postgraduate Applicant Portal (by ticking the box ‘Yes – I wish to apply for funding’ in the funding section of the portal). They must also apply by the funding deadline for their course .

There is no need to complete a separate application form for a Newnham scholarship but it will be necessary to 'opt in' to some of the scholarships on the Applicant Portal. The details for each scholarship below indicate whether it is advisable to select Newnham as a first or second choice College on the Applicant Portal.
Scholarships are awarded between April and July.
Scholarships for International or Home Fee Students
Faculty of Divinity-Newnham College PhD Scholarship in New Testament Studies (full scholarship)
One scholarship available for October 2027 entry
For a PhD in Theology and Religious Studies, focusing on New Testament Studies
For a female student of any nationality with International or Home fee status
Covers full University Composition Fee and maintenance costs at the UKRI stipend rate (£21,805 in 2026-27), as well as visa and immigration health surcharge.
There is no need to select Newnham as a first or second preference on the Applicant Portal but the successful applicant will need to accept a transfer to Newnham to take up the scholarship
Joint scholarship provided by the Faculty of Divinity’s Morna Hooker Fund and Newnham College’s Royalton-Kisch Fund.
Faculty of Divinity-Newnham College MPhil Scholarship in Medieval Islamic Philosophy (full scholarship)
Covers full University Composition Fee and pro-rata maintenance costs at the UKRI stipend rate (estimated to be £17,171 for a 9-month course in 2027-28)
Joint scholarship provided by the Faculty of Divinity’s Hartwell Fund and Newnham College’s Royalton-Kisch Fund.
Newnham MPhil Scholarship in Archaeology (maintenance stipend)
For a female student of any nationality with either International or Home fee status
Covers maintenance costs at the UKRI stipend rate (£21,805 in 2026-27; pro rata according to length of course)
Provided by the College’s Winkworth Fund
Newnham MPhil Scholarship in Geography (maintenance stipend)
Provided by the College’s Jean Mitchell Fund
Newnham MPhil Scholarship in French Language or Literature (maintenance stipend)
Covers maintenance costs at the UKRI stipend rate (estimated to be £17,171 for a 9-month course in 2027-28)
Provided by the College’s Josephine Haslewood Fund
Scholarships for International Fee Students
The HS Chau Foundation Scholarship (full STEM PhD scholarship)

This scholarship is provided by the HS Chau Foundation to support academically outstanding international female PhD students studying STEM subjects at Newnham to contribute to society by producing intellectually rigorous research which makes a positive difference to the academic community and beyond.
Two scholarships available for October 2027 entry
For a PhD in any STEM subject
For female students of any nationality with International fee status
Covers full University Composition Fee, maintenance costs at the UKRI stipend rate (£21,805 in 2026-27) and the Immigration Health Surcharge (£3,492)

There is no need to select Newnham as a first or second preference on the Applicant Portal as long as applicants accept a transfer to Newnham to take up the scholarship. However, if the field of applications is particularly competitive, preference will be given to applicants who select Newnham as their first or second choice College.
Newnham PhD Scholarship in Arts & Humanities (full scholarship)
For a PhD in any subject in the School of Arts & Humanities
For a female student of any nationality with International fee status

There is no need to select Newnham as a first or second preference on the Applicant Portal as long as the successful applicant accepts a transfer to Newnham to take up the scholarship. However, if the field of applications is particularly competitive, preference will be given to applicants who select Newnham as their first or second choice College.
City University Hong Kong Research Masters Scholarship Programme at Newnham College (full scholarship)

City University of Hong Kong (CityUHK) and Newnham College have established a new partnership to support exceptional Masters degree students from CityUHK applying to study at the University of Cambridge.

Starting in the 2025-26 academic year, two full scholarships will be awarded annually over the next five years to outstanding graduates from CityUHK commencing a full-time research Masters course at Newnham College in any discipline.
Each scholarship will cover tuition fees and maintenance for the duration of the course.
About the Scholarships CityUHK enjoys a close partnership with the Departments in the University of Cambridge on student exchange and academic collaboration.
Cambridge Australia Studentship

Thanks to the generous endowment of Professor Jan Anderson Cambridge Australia Scholarships are now offering a dedicated Newnham Studentship to a female Australian graduate intending to study for a PhD degree at Cambridge.
For details on how to apply, please contact the Cambridge Australia Scholarships .

Newnham PhD Scholarship in History (full scholarship)
For a PhD in History
For a female student with Home fee status
Covers full University Composition Fee and maintenance costs at the UKRI stipend rate (£21,805 in 2026-27)
Provided by the College’s Ruth Cohen Fund
Newnham PhD Scholarship in Chemistry (full scholarship)
For a PhD in Chemistry
Provided by the College’s Anne Logue Fund
Newnham PhD Scholarship in Modern & Medieval Languages (full scholarship)
For a PhD in Modern & Medieval Languages

For a PhD in any subject
For a female student with Home fee status with a home address within 10 miles of the former Liverpool Exchange (postcode L2 2BS)
Provided by the College’s Liverpool Clough Fund
The Jean Gooder MPhil Scholarship in English Studies (full scholarship)
For a female UK student with Home fee status
Covers full University Composition Fee and maintenance costs at the 2027-28 UKRI stipend rate (estimated to be £17,171 pro-rata for 9 months)
Newnham MPhil Scholarship in Classics (maintenance stipend)
Covers maintenance costs at the 2027-28 UKRI stipend rate (estimated to be £17,171 pro-rata for 9 months)
Provided by the College’s Baxter Fund
Newnham MPhil Scholarship in Engineering (£10,000)
Three £10,000 scholarships available for October 2027 entry
For female students of any nationality with Home fee status
Contributes £10,000 towards the overall costs of the MPhil (fees and/or maintenance)
There is no need to select Newnham as a first or second preference on the Applicant Portal but applicants will need to accept a transfer to Newnham to take up the scholarship
Provided by the College’s Steers Mardinian Fund

PhD in Astronomy

The University's minimum academic requirement for admission as a PhD student is the equivalent of a good UK 2.1 four-year undergraduate honours degree (five-year from Scottish universities). If you are studying for a degree overseas and are unsure of its UK equivalent, use the International qualifications | Postgraduate Study checker or contact The IoA Admissions Office for advice.

The Institute offers the opportunity to study for the PhD degree, for which the normal duration of study is three and a half years. The format is almost exclusively research based, although students attend a number of short courses during their first year focusing on research-related skills. The typical PhD intake each year is between 12 and 15 students.
PhD projects may be exclusively theoretical or observational but many combine aspects of both and the majority involve sophisticated data-analysis techniques.

It is normal for students to attend several relevant conferences/workshops during their period of study. Most students working on observational research projects will undertake observing trips (depending on the requirements of their project) to telescopes overseas.
Funding and Studentships

Full funding for * Home and some Republic of Ireland and Overseas-fee students is via the award of one of our Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC) Doctoral Landscape Awards. All eligible students, including those with Home- and Overseas-fee status, will be considered automatically for an STFC studentship.

A number of Overseas-fee PhD students are admitted each year, with scholarships from other sources, including the University of Cambridge, Cambridge Trust and Gates Cambridge. A few secure funding from organisations in their own country.

*For clarification, 'Home-fee' status typically applies to UK nationals and certain residents, while 'Overseas-fee' applies to international students. Please refer to this page for more information: Funding for PhD Students | Institute of Astronomy

You may also be interested in postgraduate research opportunities in Cavendish Astrophysics and the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics . A separate University application is necessary for each department where you wish to be considered for a PhD place.

While the decision regarding an offer of a PhD place is made on academic grounds, including an assessment of a student’s application and the availability of suitable projects/supervisors, for the majority of students the question of funding for the PhD is also key.

The Institute of Astronomy receives a number of STFC-funded PhD studentships each year. These cover full tuition and living costs for three and a half years and are mainly available to students with Home-fee status although a small amount may be awarded to Overseas-fee students. All eligible applicants are automatically considered. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed in late February, and those awarded a studentship will explore project and supervisor options when they begin their PhD in October 2027.
Home and Overseas students are also eligible for a range of University scholarships. To be considered, make sure to tick the “Apply for funding” box on the application form.

Applicants applying for Gates Cambridge funding , should tick the relevant box and complete the Gates Personal Statement, which should focus on leadership and helping others. You’ll also be asked to upload a research proposal ( Gates applicants only ). If you don’t yet have a project, upload a PDF that says: “The research project will be developed in collaboration with a supervisor after the application deadline.”

It’s also worth exploring funding opportunities in your home country for study abroad. Your current university may have information on available options. If you’re a strong candidate, we can help with forms that require details about research projects or supervisors.

lines: Apply to Caius
Postgraduates
Postgraduate costs
Postgraduate costs and funding

Understanding costs and funding options is a vital aspect of the application process for Postgraduates. All students are expected to have their finances in place before the start of their course, to ensure they can afford to study and live in Cambridge. At Caius, we hope to provide as much information and assistance as possible to make this process easier.
As a postgraduate student, you will have two costs to cover annually: the University Composition Fee and your Maintenance (living expenses).

The University Composition Fee (tuition fee) covers the cost of your teaching and supervision, and access to University and College facilities supporting your studies. This will vary depending on the course you are taking, and whether you are a home or overseas student.

The University webpage allows you to search for your proposed course and provides details on both home and overseas tuition fees that make up the University Composition Fee for Masters-level courses and Doctoral study for the next academic year.

Your maintenance costs may vary depending on lifestyle and your choice of course. As the circumstances of Postgraduates differ widely, the University has provided a maintenance calculator which can give you an idea of what your living costs per year will be.

Factors that affect your maintenance costs will include rent, food, entertainment, and any additional resources you will require for your course. The UKRI has a recommended minimum stipend (see the UKRI website) .
Accommodation at Caius is provided to all Postgraduates, including a guaranteed three years of accommodation for PhD students. Our accommodation is reasonably-priced and high-quality.

The Minimum Dining Requirement is a fixed charge which pays for a minimum of 16 dinner tickets each term. Each dinner ticket entitles you to a standard 3-course dinner at Caius. We aim to promote community and the exchange of ideas, as we strongly believe in the value of College members eating together regularly. You can find more information about the MDR and Postgraduate dining at Caius here.
Funding options

There are multiple sources of funding available to postgraduates. The most common sources are College Studentships, Department Awards (such as Doctoral Training Partnership awards), UKRI Studentships and Cambridge Trust or Gates Awards.

Gonville and Caius College is committed to providing opportunities for a wide range of applicants who wish to pursue fully-funded Postgraduate research, and Caius has a number of Postgraduate studentships available to candidates applying to the College.
Shubham (Law PhD 2022) talks about the importance of funding

The University’s Postgraduate Funding Search page details all collegiate, departmental and university studentships. It also includes studentships offered by affiliated funding bodies such as the Cambridge Trust , GATES Cambridge and UKRI Research Councils .

It is important to bear in mind that there are many College studentships which give preference to those who have applied to that College as their first-choice College. All Caius studentships prioritise applicants who have entered Caius as their first-choice college. Think carefully about the studentships provided by each college and which may be best suited to your course of study. The Postgraduate Funding Search should help you find the studentships offered by colleges which you are eligible for to help aid your choice.
How to apply

With the exception of the W.M. Tapp Studentship and Caius Engineering Trust Studentship, all remaining Caius Studentships are awarded in partnership with the Cambridge Trust and the UK Research Councils. As such no separate application is required. Applicants will be considered for all departmental, collegiate and University awards for which they are eligible automatically if they have selected that they wish to be considered for funding on their University postgraduate admissions application form.

Please check and apply by the funding deadline specific to your course. There are two general course deadlines of 3 December 2024 and 7 January 2025. In some cases, such as for the Research Council Doctoral Training Programmes, a separate application is required and therefore please go to the relevant website. For further information on how to apply for funding Postgraduate research in Cambridge, see here .

Priority will be given to those candidates who choose Caius as their first-choice college. The availability of Postgraduate Studentships changes from year to year and not all studentships are awarded every year. Full details of the studentships available each year is available on the University’s Funding Management Portal.
Academic & Travel Grant

All Postgraduate students at Caius can apply for support for travel and expenses related to their research on a case-by-case basis over their time at Caius. There are also language learning grants, co-curricular grants, including for music tuition, and small academic grants to which Postgraduate students can also apply.
Bell-Wade Bursary
Through the generosity of two alumni of the College, the Bell-Wade Bursary Fund has been established to assist students with the costs of pursuing excellence in sport as well as academic study.
Instrumental Awards
Music Awards

The Holland Fund exists to provide grants to students reading Music who are in financial need. The Grabowski Bursary provides money for instrumental and other musical tuition, with preference to those reading Music.
Choral Awards

Postgraduate members of the choir are entitled to three free meals in College a week and singing lessons worth up to £800. All choir members get free tours as well as CD recording and BBC Radio broadcast opportunities.

The Director of Music, Matthew Martin, encourages anyone interested joining the choir to apply by emailing Claire Wheeler ( choir@cam.ac.uk ) or him directly ( precentor@cai.cam.ac.uk ). Please detail any relevant choral or singing experience (though this is not essential) and your reasons for wanting to join the choir.

Bauer Studentship
One Bauer Studentship is intended to support an outstanding postgraduate student in any subject pursuing a Master’s degree.
This Studentship usually covers University fees at the home rate and a maintenance stipend at the UKRI recommended rate.
J.R. Bellerby Studentship in Economics
One J.R. Bellerby Award is intended to support an outstanding student pursuing a Master’s degree in Economics.
This Studentship usually covers full University fees at the home rate and a maintenance stipend at the UKRI recommended rate.
Tammy Chen Studentship
The Tammy Chen Studentship is intended to support one postgraduate student pursuing a Master's degree in the Humanities subjects at Caius.
This Studentship provides £6,000 worth of top-up funding in conjunction with the Cambridge Trust.
Richard Darlington Studentship
One Darlington Studentship is intended to support a gifted student from a Somaliland university to undertake a Master’s degree at Cambridge. Undergraduate candidates may be considered.
This Studentship covers full University fees and provides a maintenance stipend at the UKRI recommended rate.
Syn Studentships

Mr Mike Syn (1990) has generously donated money to support maintenance costs for Master's students at Caius. Wherever possible, it is preferred that the Studentships be awarded to Caius graduates with particular focus on widening participation. The recipient will be selected by the postgraduate tutors of the College based on Part II examination results.
PhD Studentships
Caius Engineering Trust Studentships

The Caius Engineering Trust Studentship is for an outstanding candidate wishing to pursue doctoral research in Engineering. The Studentship usually covers University fees and a maintenance allowance for three and a half years, and is subject to satisfactory progress in the first year.
Lord Choudrey International Studentship
The Lord Choudrey International Studentship is intended to support one outstanding PhD student from Pakistan in conjunction with the Cambridge Trust.
Phyllis Barclay-Smith Studentships
Intended to support students from Malawi but, failing this, the College will use the studentship to fund an international student in any PhD subject.
Rita Cavonius Studentship
The Rita Cavonius Studentship is intended to support one PhD student from the UK pursuing a degree in Plant Sciences.
This Studentship is intended to cover full University fees and a maintenance stipend at the UKRI recommended rate in conjunction with the NERC-DTP.
Goodhart Fund
The Goodhart Fund is intended to top-up funding received by a student undertaking a PhD where research is focused on forestry or birds.
Frank Smart Studentship
The Frank Smart Studentship is intended to support one PhD student pursuing a degree in Plant Sciences.
R.O. Whyte Studentship
The R. O. Whyte Studentship is intended for one PhD student for research in the Ecology of Monsoonal and Equatorial Asia and is tenable for three years, in partnership with the Cambridge Trust.
Shuttleworth Studentships

Awarded to candidates for admission to a PhD course, in Zoology, Physiology, or any other subject funded by the BBSRC Doctoral Training Programme. The Shuttleworth Studentship is tenable for up to three years; it normally covers University fees and also includes a maintenance allowance.
Stanley Elmore Studentship in Biomedical Sciences
Intended to support an outstanding student pursuing a PhD in the Biomedical Sciences, in partnership with the Cambridge Trust.
This Studentship is intended to cover full University fees and a maintenance stipend at the UKRI recommended rate.
Master’s and PhD Studentships
W.M. Tapp Studentships in Law

W.M. Tapp Studentships in Law are awarded annually for LLM and PhD courses in Law. Applications should be made via the application form on the W M Tapp Studentships in Law webpage . Completed applications should be submitted by 23:59 (GMT) 5 January, before starting the following October.
These Studentships tend to cover full University fees and a maintenance stipend at the UKRI recommended rate .
External Funding
There are also external funding opportunities for postgraduate study. Some useful resources include:
British Council – Study UK – provides useful information on country specific funding and funding opportunities for international students.

UK Government Postgraduate Masters & Doctoral Loans - The UK Government provides Postgraduate Loans for Masters & PhD students through a scheme administered by Student Finance England. These typically do not cover the cost of full fees and maintenance but are a contribution to your costs.
For further information about external funding, scholarships and loans, please see the University website .

lines: Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholars Programme

The aim of the Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholars Programme is to support outstanding PhD students in any discipline. At least 45 PhD students across the University of Cambridge will receive a prestigious Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholarship annually creating a cohort of the strongest PhD students in any given year across a diverse range of subject areas.

Thanks to the generosity of our alumnus David Harding (1979, Natural Sciences; Honorary Fellow 2013), through the donation from the David and Claudia Harding Foundation to St Catharine's College and the University of Cambridge, a significant proportion of the postgraduates in the Programme will be based at St Catharine’s.
Who is eligible?

Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholarships are available to candidates applying to pursue a full-time or part-time residential PhD course of study at the University of Cambridge. Scholarships are open to PhD students of any nationality and in any discipline. Find out more about elibility criteria .
What does a Harding Scholarship cover?
A Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholarship covers the following costs for PhD students:
a maintenance allowance (living costs) for the first 3.5 years of your course (£22,310 for the academic year 2026-27)
the option to request additional maintenance funding for in the final six months of the writing-up period, should this be required (i.e. up to 4 years in total).

a personal research allowance (for expenditure on personal research expenses and research-related activities, for example, books and conference attendance) of up to £6,000 over the duration of your course.

the cost of an inbound airfare, economy travel to return to your usual place of residence, visa costs and the cost of the Immigration Health Surcharge (for the duration of the visa granted), as applicable for international students.
additional discretionary funding subject to approval.
Find out more from the University's web pages about the Scholarship.
A calendar of activities and academic events will also be available to Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholars over the course of each academic year.
How can I apply?

You can apply for admission to a PhD course, a College place and various sources of funding via the University’s Postgraduate Applicant Portal. Full details can be found on the Postgraduate Admissions website .

When making your online application, please ensure you indicate that you wish to be considered for funding and complete the funding section. Applicants who do not complete this section will not be considered for Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholarships.
When do applications open and how long are they open for?

Harding Distinguished Postgraduate Scholarships are awarded as part of the University’s Postgraduate Funding Competition so, as per the terms of the competition, the application deadline is determined by the funding deadline for the PhD course they are applying to. Find out more about the application process.
